purpose: machine-readable ontology of concrete public-speaking and delivery work-units spanning message design (rhetoric, storytelling, rule of three, the hook), talk structure (opening, throughline, call to action, memorability), delivery and performance (voice, pacing, body language, eye contact, slides as support), and nerves and Q&A (stage fright, rehearsal, handling questions), as a subdomain node of professional communication & speaking for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Public speaking and delivery is modeled as a subdomain of professional communication and speaking.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable speaking/presentation work-units, not topics to read about.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows Anderson (2016, TED Talks: The Official TED Guide to Public Speaking) and Heath & Heath (2007, Made to Stick).
exclusions: Written communication, copywriting, and non-spoken document design.
Broadcast/podcast production engineering and audio post-production.
Debate adjudication and formal competitive-debate rule systems.
Subject-matter fact-checking of the talk's domain claims.

competency_questions.question: Who is the audience and what single change in belief or action should the talk produce?
What is the one-sentence core message the whole talk is built around?
How is persuasive weight balanced across credibility, emotion, and logic for this audience?
Which concrete stories carry the idea, and how is it made memorable and sticky?
How does the opening seize attention and frame the talk's promise?
How are points grouped (rule of three) and repetitions used for memorability of structure?
In what order do sections run and how are transitions signposted into a coherent arc?
How does the close resolve the throughline and ask for one concrete action?
How do slides support rather than duplicate speech, and should the speaker script, outline, or memorize?
How do voice, body language, and eye contact reinforce the message and connect with the room?
How is the talk rehearsed to fluency and fitted to the allotted time with cut/expand options?
How are nerves managed and audience questions, including hostile or unknown ones, handled without losing the message?
How are room, AV, and tech verified, and end-to-end readiness validated by a full dress run before going live?
How is the delivered talk reviewed to improve the next one?

glossary.definition: the single connecting idea every part of the talk supports
persuasion through the speaker's perceived credibility and character
persuasion through engaging the audience's emotion
persuasion through logical argument and evidence
the opening device that seizes attention in the first seconds
grouping ideas or phrases in threes for memorability
the closing request for one concrete change in the audience
the property of an idea that makes it memorable and transmissible
the speaker's difficulty imagining not knowing what they know
the principle that visuals reinforce the speaker, not replace them
performance anxiety experienced before or during speaking
redirecting a question back toward the core message
a full end-to-end rehearsal under near-live conditions
explicit cues that tell the audience where they are in the talk

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established public-speaking and message-design literature (Anderson 2016, TED Talks; Heath & Heath 2007, Made to Stick) and analytic practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Profile the specific audience, occasion, and the single change in belief or action the talk must produce.
contradictors: speaker who talks about what interests only themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the audience, venue, or talk objective changes

pros.claim: everything downstream is shaped to one audience and one goal
pros.example: tailoring the same idea for engineers vs investors changes the whole talk

cons.claim: a wrong audience model misdirects every later choice
cons.example: designing for experts when the room is beginners

failure_modes: purpose stated as a topic, not a change
acceptance_tests: purpose is one sentence naming a change in the audience
audience profile cites the actual room, not a generic persona
revisit_triggers: new constraints on length or format

nodes.definition: Compress the talk into one sentence the audience should remember, the throughline every part connects to.

included: what to cut that does not serve it

contradictors: speaker who tries to convey everything they know

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the purpose changes or the throughline fails to connect a section

pros.claim: a single throughline gives the talk unity and memorability
pros.example: Anderson's advice: one major idea built across the talk

cons.claim: forcing a complex topic into one idea can oversimplify
cons.example: reducing a research program to a slogan loses nuance

failure_modes: throughline too abstract to test sections against
acceptance_tests: core message expressible in one spoken sentence
each planned section demonstrably serves the throughline
revisit_triggers: a section cannot be tied to the throughline

nodes.definition: Allocate persuasive weight across speaker credibility, emotional resonance, and logical argument for this audience.
contradictors: speaker who relies on data alone for a lay audience

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when audience disposition or the evidence base changes

pros.claim: matching appeals to the audience raises persuasion
pros.example: a skeptical board needs ethos and logos before pathos

cons.claim: over-weighting pathos can read as manipulation
cons.example: an emotional plea with no evidence erodes trust with experts

failure_modes: all logos for an audience that needs ethos first
acceptance_tests: each appeal type is present in proportion justified by the audience
credibility is established before the main ask

nodes.definition: Design concrete stories with character, stakes, and turn that carry the abstract idea emotionally.

included: connecting the story to the point

contradictors: presenter who lists facts with no narrative

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the core message shifts or a story tests as confusing

pros.claim: stories make ideas concrete, emotional, and memorable
pros.example: a single patient's story lands a public-health statistic

cons.claim: a vivid story can overshadow or distort the point
cons.example: the audience remembers the anecdote but not the conclusion

failure_modes: story that does not connect to the point
story so long it crowds out the argument
acceptance_tests: each story explicitly maps to a point in the throughline
story length is justified by its payload

nodes.definition: Craft the first 30-60 seconds to seize attention and frame the talk's promise.
contradictors: speaker who opens with an agenda slide and thanks

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the core message or opening material changes

pros.claim: a strong hook earns the audience's attention for the rest
pros.example: opening with a surprising fact or vivid scene beats a recap

cons.claim: a gimmicky hook can misframe a serious talk
cons.example: a shock opener that the body never pays off feels like a trick

acceptance_tests: opening reaches the hook within the first minute
the promise made in the opening is delivered later

nodes.definition: Use triadic grouping and repetition patterns to make structure graspable and lines memorable.
contradictors: speaker with a flat list of nine equal points

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when sections are re-grouped or key lines are rewritten

pros.claim: triads are easy to follow and recall
pros.example: 'government of the people, by the people, for the people'

cons.claim: forcing threes can pad or distort real structure
cons.example: inventing a third point only to complete a triad

acceptance_tests: groupings of three are genuine, not padded
repetitions are deliberate and bounded

nodes.definition: Sequence opening, throughline development, and resolution into a coherent arc with signposted transitions.
contradictors: speaker who jumps between topics without transitions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when sections are added, cut, or reordered

pros.claim: a clear arc lets the audience follow without getting lost
pros.example: signposted transitions tell the audience where they are

cons.claim: a rigid structure can feel mechanical
cons.example: over-signposting ('my third point is') can deaden a talk

failure_modes: sections in an order that breaks the logic
acceptance_tests: each transition connects the prior section to the next
the arc builds toward the core message and CTA

nodes.definition: Design a closing that resolves the throughline and asks the audience for one concrete change.
contradictors: speaker who ends with 'that's all, questions?'

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the purpose or the desired action changes

pros.claim: a clear ask converts attention into the intended change
pros.example: ending with one specific action beats a vague 'think about it'

cons.claim: multiple asks dilute the close
cons.example: ending with five action items leaves none salient

failure_modes: close that does not resolve the opening
acceptance_tests: the close states exactly one primary action
the close resolves the opening promise

nodes.definition: Apply stickiness principles (simple, unexpected, concrete, credible, emotional, story) so the idea survives after the talk.

included: concreteness and the curse of knowledge

contradictors: speaker who buries the idea in abstraction and jargon

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the core message or supporting claims change

pros.claim: stickiness makes the idea spread and persist
pros.example: 'Made to Stick' SUCCESs turns a claim into a memorable one

cons.claim: chasing unexpectedness can sacrifice accuracy
cons.example: a catchy but misleading frame distorts the point

failure_modes: curse-of-knowledge abstraction the audience cannot picture
acceptance_tests: the core idea is concrete and pictureable
at least one unexpected, credible element is present

nodes.definition: Build visuals that reinforce, not duplicate, the spoken words and never become the speaker's script.
contradictors: speaker who reads bullet-dense slides aloud

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when content changes or slides start duplicating speech

pros.claim: visuals add evidence and emotion words cannot
pros.example: a photograph or chart can carry what a sentence cannot

cons.claim: text-heavy slides split attention and replace the speaker
cons.example: reading slides makes the speaker redundant

acceptance_tests: no slide functions as the speaker's script
each visual carries information speech cannot

nodes.definition: Decide between fully scripting, bullet-outlining, or memorizing, matched to the speaker and stakes.

included: script vs outline vs memorize tradeoff

contradictors: speaker who memorizes verbatim and freezes on a slip

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the speaker's comfort or rehearsal outcome changes the plan

pros.claim: matching format to the speaker reduces freeze risk
pros.example: an outline keeps a talk conversational while a script ensures precision

cons.claim: verbatim memorization is brittle under stress
cons.example: a single forgotten word can derail a memorized talk

failure_modes: over-reliance on a full script killing eye contact
acceptance_tests: the chosen format suits the speaker's experience and the stakes
a fallback exists if memory fails

nodes.definition: Control pace, pitch, volume, and silence so the voice conveys meaning and emphasis.
contradictors: speaker who rushes in a flat monotone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the script or timing changes, or rehearsal flags pacing issues

pros.claim: vocal variety holds attention and signals meaning
pros.example: a deliberate pause before the key line lands it

cons.claim: over-rehearsed delivery can sound artificial
cons.example: exaggerated intonation reads as insincere

acceptance_tests: pace and pauses are marked at key moments
vocal variety is present without sounding artificial

nodes.definition: Use posture, gesture, movement, and stage position to reinforce the message and project presence.
contradictors: speaker who paces nervously or hides behind a lectern

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the venue layout or blocking changes

pros.claim: purposeful movement adds emphasis and energy
pros.example: stepping toward the audience on the key ask increases impact

cons.claim: aimless movement and fidgeting distract
cons.example: pacing back and forth signals nerves not confidence

acceptance_tests: movement is purposeful and tied to content
distracting habits are identified and curbed

nodes.definition: Establish and sustain eye contact to build connection, read the room, and adjust in real time.

included: reading and responding to the room

contradictors: speaker who stares at slides or notes throughout

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the delivery format or room layout changes

pros.claim: eye contact builds trust and lets the speaker read the room
pros.example: scanning faces reveals confusion to address live

cons.claim: forced or scanning gaze can feel mechanical
cons.example: a fixed sweep pattern looks robotic

failure_modes: eyes locked on notes or slides
gaze that never rests on a person
acceptance_tests: eye contact is distributed across the room
the speaker can read and respond to audience signals

nodes.definition: Run structured rehearsals with feedback and revision until the talk is fluent and within time.
contradictors: speaker who reads it through once silently the night before

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when content or delivery plans change after a rehearsal

pros.claim: rehearsal converts a plan into fluent, timed delivery
pros.example: rehearsing aloud surfaces awkward transitions a read-through hides

cons.claim: over-rehearsal can make delivery stale or memorized-brittle
cons.example: drilling a script word-for-word kills spontaneity

acceptance_tests: the talk is rehearsed aloud to time at least once
feedback from a rehearsal is incorporated

nodes.definition: Apply preparation and in-the-moment techniques to convert anxiety into manageable, even useful, energy.
contradictors: speaker who tries to suppress all nerves and panics when they appear

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a rehearsal or prior talk reveals new anxiety triggers

pros.claim: managed arousal sharpens focus and presence
pros.example: reframing 'I'm nervous' as 'I'm excited' improves performance

cons.claim: over-managing nerves can flatten energy and authenticity
cons.example: numbing all arousal removes the edge that energizes a talk

failure_modes: panic spiral with no recovery plan
suppression that backfires into a freeze
acceptance_tests: a concrete pre-talk and in-the-moment routine exists
a recovery technique is rehearsed for a freeze or blank

nodes.definition: Prepare for and manage audience questions, including hostile or off-topic ones, without losing the message.
contradictors: speaker who is defensive or rambles in answers

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the message or anticipated question set changes

pros.claim: strong Q&A protects and extends the message
pros.example: bridging a loaded question back to the core point keeps control

cons.claim: over-bridging can read as evasive
cons.example: dodging every question erodes credibility

failure_modes: bluffing an answer the speaker does not know
acceptance_tests: likely and hostile questions are anticipated with answers
a credible fallback exists for unknown answers

nodes.definition: Fit the talk to the allotted time with cut/expand options and a plan for running over or under.
contradictors: speaker who routinely runs 50% over and gets cut off

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the slot length or content length changes

pros.claim: a timing plan prevents being cut off before the point
pros.example: pre-marked cut modules let a speaker recover lost time

cons.claim: aggressive cutting can drop the throughline payoff
cons.example: cutting the close to save time loses the whole point

failure_modes: talk that overruns and loses the close
acceptance_tests: a timed run-through fits the slot with margin
cut/expand modules are pre-identified and ranked

nodes.definition: Verify room, audio-visual, slides, and contingency so technical failure cannot break the talk.
contradictors: speaker who first sees the room as they walk on stage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the venue, deck, or AV equipment changes

pros.claim: verified tech removes a common failure mode
pros.example: a sound and clicker check pre-talk avoids on-stage scrambling

cons.claim: over-reliance on tech leaves no fallback
cons.example: a deck-only talk dies if the projector fails

failure_modes: slides that do not display correctly in the room
acceptance_tests: AV, slides, and mic are verified in the actual room
an analog fallback exists for total tech failure

nodes.definition: Run a full dress rehearsal that validates content, delivery, timing, and tech coherence before going live.
contradictors: speaker who skips the dress run and improvises live

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any upstream content, delivery, timing, or tech artifact changes

pros.claim: a dress run catches integration failures a partial rehearsal misses
pros.example: a full run reveals that the talk runs long and the close is rushed

cons.claim: a late dry run leaves no time to fix what it finds
cons.example: discovering a structural problem the night before is too late

failure_modes: readiness asserted without a full dress run
defects found but not fixed before go-live
acceptance_tests: a full dress run-through is completed end to end
every defect found is triaged before the go decision
revisit_triggers: any upstream artifact changes after the dry run
timing or tech fails in the dress run

nodes.definition: Capture recording, audience response, and self-review after the talk to improve the next one.
contradictors: speaker who never reviews a recording or feedback

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: after each delivered talk or when new feedback arrives

pros.claim: structured review compounds skill across talks
pros.example: reviewing a recording reveals filler words to cut next time

cons.claim: ungrounded self-criticism can demoralize rather than improve
cons.example: fixating on minor flaws ignores what worked

failure_modes: no review of recording or feedback
acceptance_tests: a recording or structured feedback is reviewed
at least one prioritized improvement is recorded

edges.why_related: the core message is distilled for the analyzed audience and purpose
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tailoring the idea to the room
edges.risk_of_conflict: a wrong audience model misdirects the message
edges.example: know the room before fixing the one idea
edges.resolution_rule: fix audience and purpose before distilling the message

edges.why_related: appeals are allocated to carry the core message
edges.risk_of_conflict: balancing appeals before fixing the message wastes effort
edges.example: decide the idea, then how to persuade
edges.resolution_rule: distill the message before allocating appeals

edges.why_related: stories are chosen to deliver the planned emotional and credibility appeals
edges.risk_of_conflict: writing stories before the appeal mix risks off-tone material
edges.example: plan the appeal mix, then pick stories
edges.resolution_rule: set the appeal balance before writing stories

edges.why_related: triads group the points that serve the core message
edges.risk_of_conflict: patterning before the message can invent filler
edges.example: fix the points, then group in threes
edges.resolution_rule: distill the message before patterning

edges.why_related: the opening often draws on a chosen story or scene
edges.risk_of_conflict: designing the hook before stories risks a disconnected opener
edges.example: choose stories, then craft the hook
edges.resolution_rule: select stories before designing the hook

edges.why_related: stickiness is engineered around the distilled core idea
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying stickiness before the idea is fixed targets the wrong claim
edges.example: fix the idea, then make it stick
edges.resolution_rule: distill the message before engineering stickiness

edges.why_related: the arc begins from the designed opening
edges.risk_of_conflict: sequencing before the opening risks reworking the start
edges.example: design the opening, then sequence the arc
edges.resolution_rule: design the hook before sequencing the arc

edges.why_related: triadic groupings inform the section sequence
edges.risk_of_conflict: sequencing without grouping yields a flat list
edges.example: group in threes, then sequence
edges.resolution_rule: group points before sequencing the arc

edges.why_related: the close resolves the arc into a single ask
edges.risk_of_conflict: writing the CTA before the arc risks a disconnected close
edges.example: build the arc, then design the close
edges.resolution_rule: sequence the arc before designing the CTA

edges.why_related: slides are built to support the sequenced sections
edges.risk_of_conflict: building slides before the arc forces rework
edges.example: fix the arc, then build slides
edges.resolution_rule: sequence the arc before building slides

edges.why_related: the note format is chosen for the completed arc
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing format before the arc is premature
edges.example: fix the arc, then choose note format
edges.resolution_rule: sequence the arc before choosing script vs outline

edges.why_related: vocal pacing is planned against the chosen script or outline
edges.risk_of_conflict: pacing without a fixed format gets reworked
edges.example: choose the format, then plan the voice
edges.resolution_rule: decide script vs outline before planning vocal delivery

edges.why_related: gesture and movement are coordinated with vocal emphasis
edges.risk_of_conflict: blocking without vocal cues desynchronizes delivery
edges.example: plan the voice, then the body
edges.resolution_rule: plan vocal emphasis before blocking the body

edges.why_related: eye contact depends on how much the speaker reads from notes
edges.risk_of_conflict: planning gaze before format is premature
edges.example: choose the format, then plan eye contact
edges.resolution_rule: decide note reliance before planning eye contact

edges.why_related: rehearsal runs the talk with the actual slides
edges.risk_of_conflict: rehearsing without final slides hides handoff issues
edges.example: finalize slides, then rehearse with them
edges.resolution_rule: build slides before rehearsing with them

edges.why_related: rehearsal drills the planned vocal delivery
edges.risk_of_conflict: rehearsing without a voice plan wastes reps
edges.example: plan the voice, then rehearse it
edges.resolution_rule: plan vocal delivery before rehearsing

edges.why_related: rehearsal builds the fluency that reduces nerves and reveals triggers
edges.risk_of_conflict: building a nerves routine without rehearsal data is guesswork
edges.example: rehearse, then tune the nerves routine
edges.resolution_rule: rehearse before finalizing the nerves routine

edges.why_related: Q&A prep is rehearsed alongside the talk
edges.risk_of_conflict: unrehearsed Q&A collapses under pressure
edges.example: rehearse the talk, then drill Q&A
edges.resolution_rule: rehearse before drilling Q&A

edges.why_related: timed run-throughs produce the timing plan
edges.risk_of_conflict: timing without run-throughs is theoretical
edges.example: rehearse to time, then build the timing plan
edges.resolution_rule: rehearse to time before fixing the timing plan

edges.why_related: tech setup verifies the actual deck in the room
edges.risk_of_conflict: setup without the final deck misses display issues
edges.example: finalize slides, then verify tech
edges.resolution_rule: build slides before verifying tech

edges.why_related: the dry-run gate consumes a fully rehearsed talk
edges.risk_of_conflict: gating without rehearsal cannot judge readiness
edges.example: rehearse, then run the dress gate
edges.resolution_rule: rehearse before the dry-run gate

edges.why_related: the gate verifies the talk fits time
edges.risk_of_conflict: gating without a timing plan misses overruns
edges.example: fix timing, then gate readiness
edges.resolution_rule: fix timing before the dry-run gate

edges.why_related: the gate confirms tech works end to end
edges.risk_of_conflict: gating without tech checks risks live AV failure
edges.example: verify tech, then gate readiness
edges.resolution_rule: verify tech before the dry-run gate

edges.why_related: the gate confirms Q&A readiness alongside the talk
edges.risk_of_conflict: gating without Q&A prep leaves the riskiest segment untested
edges.example: prep Q&A, then gate readiness
edges.resolution_rule: prep Q&A before the dry-run gate

edges.why_related: the feedback loop runs after the gated talk is delivered
edges.risk_of_conflict: reviewing before delivery has nothing to assess
edges.example: deliver the gated talk, then review
edges.resolution_rule: pass the gate and deliver before reviewing

edges.why_related: chasing an unexpected, sticky frame can pull a story away from accuracy
edges.risk_of_conflict: a memorable frame distorts the true story
edges.example: exaggerating a story to make it stick
edges.resolution_rule: accuracy of the story dominates; stickiness must not falsify it

edges.why_related: rich storytelling expands the talk against a fixed time budget
edges.risk_of_conflict: a long story crowds out the argument and overruns
edges.example: a five-minute anecdote in a ten-minute slot
edges.resolution_rule: time budget dominates; cut or compress stories to fit

edges.why_related: heavy reliance on a full script competes with sustained eye contact
edges.risk_of_conflict: reading a script kills audience connection
edges.example: eyes glued to a script throughout
edges.resolution_rule: audience connection dominates; reduce note reliance to the minimum that is safe

edges.why_related: maximizing pathos-driven stickiness can unbalance the logos the audience needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: an emotional sticky hook with no evidence loses experts
edges.example: a catchy slogan replacing the argument
edges.resolution_rule: the audience-justified appeal balance dominates over raw stickiness

edges.why_related: managing slides competes with attention to the audience
edges.risk_of_conflict: slide-driven delivery breaks eye contact
edges.example: turning to read each slide
edges.resolution_rule: the speaker, not the slides, leads; slides must not capture the gaze

edges.why_related: the audience profile bounds which appeals are legitimate and effective
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the profile mismatches appeals to the room
edges.example: using heavy pathos for a data-driven board
edges.resolution_rule: the audience profile limits the appeal mix; do not exceed what the room accepts

edges.why_related: the stated purpose bounds what the close may ask for
edges.risk_of_conflict: an ask unrelated to the purpose confuses the audience
edges.example: asking for X when the purpose was Y
edges.resolution_rule: the talk purpose limits the CTA; the ask must serve the stated change

edges.why_related: the time budget bounds how many slides can be meaningfully shown
edges.risk_of_conflict: too many slides for the time rushes every visual
edges.example: sixty slides in a ten-minute talk
edges.resolution_rule: the time budget limits the slide count; cut slides that cannot be given time

edges.why_related: rehearsal can reveal structural problems that send the arc back for revision
edges.risk_of_conflict: a rehearsal that exposes a broken arc forces re-sequencing
edges.example: a run-through where the order confuses listeners
edges.resolution_rule: revisit the arc when rehearsal exposes a structural defect; stop when a clean timed run passes

edges.why_related: rehearsal can reveal the core message is not landing, triggering re-distillation
edges.risk_of_conflict: a run-through where listeners miss the point forces re-distillation
edges.example: testers cannot restate the one idea
edges.resolution_rule: revisit the core message when rehearsal shows it does not land; stop when testers can restate it

edges.why_related: the dry run can fail timing and send the timing plan back for revision
edges.risk_of_conflict: a dress run that overruns forces timing cuts
edges.example: a full run that lands two minutes long
edges.resolution_rule: revisit the timing plan when the dry run overruns; stop when a full run fits with margin

edges.why_related: post-talk lessons feed back into how the next talk is rehearsed
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring post-talk lessons repeats the same delivery flaws
edges.example: filler-word habit recurring across talks
edges.resolution_rule: revisit rehearsal practice with the prior talk's lessons; stop when the targeted flaw no longer recurs

edges.why_related: stickiness audits are best done before locking the section sequence
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sequencing benefits from a stickiness pass
edges.risk_of_conflict: sequencing first can bury the sticky elements
edges.example: placing the most memorable point where it is lost
edges.resolution_rule: run the stickiness pass before locking the arc when both are open

edges.why_related: vocal and physical delivery are sibling performance skills coached together
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them hides that each needs separate drilling
edges.example: treating gesture and voice as one undifferentiated skill
edges.resolution_rule: treat as related performance skills but drill voice and body separately

conflict_axes.trigger: making the idea catchy competes with keeping it true and balanced
resolution_order: make it memorable without changing its meaning
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: accuracy dominates; stickiness must not distort the claim or the evidence balance
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a memorable frame would mislead the audience
conflict_axes.example: a slogan that overstates what the evidence supports

conflict_axes.trigger: rich stories expand the talk against a fixed slot
resolution_order: keep the shortest version that delivers it
cut stories that cannot earn their time
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the time budget dominates; stories are compressed or cut to fit the slot
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if cutting a story would remove a load-bearing point
conflict_axes.example: a vivid anecdote that pushes the talk over time

conflict_axes.trigger: reading from a full script competes with sustained eye contact
resolution_order: choose the lightest notes that prevent a freeze
keep eyes on the room at key moments
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: audience connection dominates; note reliance is reduced to the safe minimum
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if reducing notes risks a memory freeze on a high-stakes passage
conflict_axes.example: eyes on the script through the entire close

conflict_axes.trigger: slide-driven delivery competes with the speaker leading the room
resolution_order: look at the room, not the screen
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the speaker leads; slides remain subordinate support
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the deck has become the de facto script
conflict_axes.example: turning away to read each slide

conflict_axes.trigger: over-rehearsal can make delivery stale or brittle, losing natural presence
resolution_order: avoid verbatim memorization of the whole talk
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: rehearse to fluency but preserve responsiveness; do not over-drill into rigidity
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if rehearsal has made the talk sound recited

conflict_axes.trigger: technical depth competes with being understood by the actual audience
resolution_order: include only the depth that serves the one idea
make the rest concrete or cut it
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: accessibility for the actual audience dominates; depth beyond their need is cut
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if required depth exceeds what the audience can follow
conflict_axes.example: jargon-dense slides for a lay audience

conflict_axes.trigger: expansive, dynamic delivery can stretch the talk past its slot
resolution_order: cut content, not pace, to recover time
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: time control dominates; presence must fit within the timing plan
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if dynamic delivery routinely overruns the slot
conflict_axes.example: dramatic pauses that push the talk long

conflict_axes.trigger: a thorough late dress run competes with leaving time to fix what it finds
resolution_order: schedule the dress run early enough to fix defects
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: readiness dominates; the dress run is scheduled to leave repair time, never skipped for the schedule
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the dress run is too late to fix discovered defects
conflict_axes.example: finding a broken arc the night before

edge_cases.trigger: sections do not connect to one core idea
edge_cases.detection_method: check each section maps to the stated throughline
resolution: cut or re-anchor sections that do not serve it

edge_cases.trigger: slides carry the full text the speaker reads
edge_cases.detection_method: check no slide contains the speaker's full script

edge_cases.trigger: the talk runs long and the close is rushed or cut
edge_cases.example: running out of time before the ask
edge_cases.detection_method: time a full run and compare to the slot

edge_cases.trigger: AV fails and there is no analog fallback
edge_cases.example: projector dies with no printout or plan
edge_cases.detection_method: verify an analog fallback exists for total AV failure

edge_cases.trigger: a hostile question is answered defensively or off-message
edge_cases.example: taking the bait on a loaded question
edge_cases.detection_method: review anticipated hostile questions and bridges
resolution: bridge back to the core message

edge_cases.trigger: a verbatim-memorized talk freezes on a forgotten word
edge_cases.example: losing the next line and stalling
edge_cases.detection_method: check a fallback and recovery technique exist

edge_cases.trigger: a third point is invented only to complete a triad
edge_cases.example: a weak third item added for symmetry
edge_cases.detection_method: check each grouped point is genuine, not padding
resolution: keep two genuine points if no real third exists

edge_cases.trigger: self-review fixates on minor flaws and ignores what worked
edge_cases.example: obsessing over filler words while ignoring strong delivery
edge_cases.detection_method: check the review records strengths and prioritized fixes

edge_cases.trigger: a stickiness/story tradeoff is modeled as a prerequisite, not a conflict
edge_cases.example: treating 'make it stick' as a hard prerequisite of storytelling
edge_cases.detection_method: check tradeoffs are conflict edges with signed_tension<0
resolution: model the tradeoff as a conflict edge

edge_cases.trigger: the talk is declared final before a full dress run passes
edge_cases.example: printing the deck before the dress run
edge_cases.detection_method: check no hard lock precedes a passed dress run
resolution: run the dress gate before locking

workflow.objective: fix the audience, purpose, and one core message
acceptance_tests: purpose names a change in the audience
the core message is one sentence
exit_criteria: audience, purpose, and core message fixed
workflow.do_first_because: nothing downstream is valid unless the audience, goal, and one idea are fixed first

workflow.objective: design the persuasion mix, stories, and stickiness around the core idea
acceptance_tests: each appeal type is justified by the audience
each story maps to a point
workflow.do_first_because: the persuasive content must be shaped before it can be sequenced

workflow.objective: build the opening, arc, and close into a coherent structure
acceptance_tests: each transition connects sections
the close states one action
workflow.do_first_because: delivery and visuals can only be planned once the structure is fixed

workflow.objective: build supporting slides and choose the note format
acceptance_tests: no slide is the speaker's script
the format suits the speaker and stakes
workflow.do_first_because: slides and note format follow the fixed structure to avoid rework

workflow.objective: plan voice, body, and eye-contact delivery
acceptance_tests: pace and pauses marked
movement is purposeful
workflow.do_first_because: performance technique is planned against the structure and note format

workflow.objective: rehearse aloud to fluency and time, producing the timing plan
acceptance_tests: rehearsed aloud to time at least once
a timed run fits with margin
workflow.do_first_because: rehearsal must operationalize all plans and surface defects before the dress run

workflow.objective: prepare nerves management and Q&A handling
acceptance_tests: a pre-talk and recovery routine exists
hostile questions have bridges
workflow.do_first_because: nerves and Q&A readiness depend on a rehearsed talk and the fixed message

workflow.objective: verify room, AV, slides, and tech contingency
acceptance_tests: AV and slides verified in the room
an analog fallback exists
workflow.do_first_because: tech must be verified before the dress run can confirm end-to-end readiness

workflow.objective: run a full dress run, decide go/no-go, then review after delivery
acceptance_tests: a full dress run completed end to end
every defect triaged before go
exit_criteria: readiness validated; talk delivered and reviewed
workflow.do_first_because: end-to-end readiness is validated last, only after all upstream artifacts pass

priority_rationale.notes: sets the persuasion mix for content
stories feed the hook and stickiness
stickiness pass before locking the arc
the close that resolves the arc
voice plan feeds body and rehearsal
review compounds skill for the next talk

dominance_rules.trigger: a memorable frame would distort the claim
dominance_rules.rule: accuracy of the claim dominates over making it catchy
dominance_rules.required_action: keep the true meaning; make it memorable only within accuracy
dominance_rules.example: trimming a slogan that overstated the evidence

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk node could be rushed to save time
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed for high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests and human review before proceeding
dominance_rules.example: not skipping the dress run to save an afternoon

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is tempting to do before its prerequisites
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates raw value ordering
dominance_rules.required_action: schedule prerequisites first even if a later node feels higher value
dominance_rules.example: fixing the core message before designing slides

dominance_rules.trigger: heavy note reliance threatens eye contact
dominance_rules.rule: audience connection dominates over note reliance
dominance_rules.required_action: reduce notes to the safe minimum and keep eyes on the room
dominance_rules.example: not reading the close off a script

dominance_rules.rule: the time budget dominates over content volume
dominance_rules.required_action: cut pre-marked modules, never the close, to fit
dominance_rules.example: dropping a secondary example to protect the ask

dominance_rules.trigger: readiness is asserted before tests pass
dominance_rules.required_action: do not hard-lock until the dress run and gates pass
dominance_rules.example: keeping the deck in draft until the dress run passes

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk choice is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-risk or irreversible choices
dominance_rules.required_action: route the decision to a reviewer with a decision record
dominance_rules.example: a coach signs off before a high-stakes keynote

dominance_rules.rule: correct evidence labeling dominates apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels; do not imply observed certainty
dominance_rules.example: labeling all priors heuristic, not observed

dominance_rules.rule: schema stability dominates raw object volume
dominance_rules.required_action: stop adding objects that break required structure
dominance_rules.example: not padding nodes past genuine distinctness

dominance_rules.trigger: an object is created without traceable grounding
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence_refs and CQ links to every object
dominance_rules.example: every node cites SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR and a CQ

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix audience and purpose before distilling the message
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a message built for the wrong room is reworked wholesale
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: the core message changes after the audience is re-understood
anti_rework_rules.example: writing a slogan before knowing the room

anti_rework_rules.rule: distill the core message before designing appeals, stories, and stickiness
anti_rework_rules.rationale: content built without a throughline gets cut or re-anchored
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: stories that do not serve any fixed idea
anti_rework_rules.example: writing anecdotes before fixing the point

anti_rework_rules.rule: design the message content before sequencing the arc
anti_rework_rules.rationale: sequencing empty sections forces re-sequencing later
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an arc reordered every time a story changes
anti_rework_rules.example: ordering sections before the stories exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the arc before building slides
anti_rework_rules.rationale: slides built to a moving structure are rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rebuilding the deck after each reorder
anti_rework_rules.example: designing slides before the order is set

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the arc before choosing script vs outline
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a note format chosen for a changing structure is redone
anti_rework_rules.example: scripting before the order is final

anti_rework_rules.rationale: rehearsing without plans ingrains random delivery
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: drilling habits that must be unlearned
anti_rework_rules.example: rehearsing before any pacing or blocking is decided

anti_rework_rules.rule: rehearse to time before fixing the timing plan
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a timing plan with no measured runs is fiction
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: cut decisions based on guessed durations
anti_rework_rules.example: planning cuts before any timed run

anti_rework_rules.rationale: verifying a draft deck misses real display issues
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: display problems found only on stage

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass a full dress run before declaring the talk final
blocked_until: dress run passed and defects triaged
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before a dress run means defects surface live
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a structural defect discovered on stage
anti_rework_rules.example: printing the deck before the dress run

anti_rework_rules.rule: model tradeoffs as conflicts before writing dominance rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: dominance rules without conflict axes are ungrounded
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a resolution rule with no named tension
anti_rework_rules.example: writing 'time wins' before defining the story-vs-time conflict

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or dress run reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by go-live risk and severity
action: score defects by risk and severity
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect is first

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
acceptance_tests: all dependents identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a prioritized defect is ready to fix
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to repair owner via repair_routing
action: route the defect to its subsystem
acceptance_tests: repair recorded with owner

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and affected checks
acceptance_tests: target check now passes
no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new feedback or rehearsal evidence changes a node's standing
iteration_protocol.detection: compare posterior delta to the revisit threshold
acceptance_tests: posteriors recomputed for affected nodes
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no node exceeds the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changed after a downstream soft/hard lock
acceptance_tests: no dependent stays locked above its upstream

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible decision is reached
acceptance_tests: a reviewer signed off with a record

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version's metrics and checks
acceptance_tests: no check regressed without justification

human_review_required_for: go/no-go decision before a high-stakes talk
hard lock of the finalized talk
handling of hostile or sensitive Q&A

checks.repair_action: modeled stickiness/story/time tensions as conflict edges, not dependencies
recomputed all derived fields via formula script

test_cases.input_summary: a talk with several unrelated points
expected_properties: each section maps to the throughline

test_cases.input_summary: a rich story in a short slot
a high-stakes talk with hostile questions
a talk locked before a dress run
expected_properties: no hard lock before the gate passes

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked talk change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade on a failed dress run
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: hard lock of the finalized talk
